summary: Shigeo Yokoyama studied at Kyoto University (~1973–1983) and worked in religious studies. He held posts at Okayama University (~1991–1997) and Nara Women's University (~1997–2019).

Shigeru Gorai was a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1929–1932) and Kyoto University (~1936–1939). His posts included Otani University (1955–1978) and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1964–1993).
Shigeru Kato worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1903) and later held a post there (~1925–1941).

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1961) and Harvard University (~1963–1967). He held posts at Tenri University (~1968–1980) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1980–2003).
Shih-Hsiang Chen worked in Sinology, studying at Peking University (~1931–1935). He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1945–1971) and taught Gary Snyder.
Shikaripur N. Sridhar works in linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at Stony Brook University, including Chair (attested 2007) and Director of the Center for India Studies (attested 2026).
Shikazo Mori was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later held a post at Bukkyo University (~1970–1979).

Shikha Rajpurohit specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (2009–2012) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (2014–2022). In 2024, she became an Assistant Professor at Krea University.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Boone University (~1920–1922) and Peking University (1923–1955).

Shilpa Sumant is an Indology scholar who earned her Ph.D. from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2000–2007). She held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (2009) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2020–2025).

Shimei Futabatei studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. Working in linguistics, he held posts at the Army War College (~1897–1899), Tokyo School of Foreign Languages (~1899–1902), and several newspapers.
Shimin Geng worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1953) and held a post there from ~1953 to 1999.
Shin Fujinaga works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts attested at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (1991, 2000) and Hiroshima University (1992).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami at Kyoto University (1912–1947). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1943–1953) and visited Harvard University in 1958.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He founded the Kindai Pyramido Kyokai and held a professorship attested at National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College in 2015.

Shin'ya Yasutomi specialized in Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Waseda University and Otani University. He held academic posts at Otani University (~1996–2010, 2014) and directed the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute (~2014–2017).
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1934). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1964–1977) and Hanazono University (~1977–1983).

Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Tohoku University and Rissho University under scholars including Ensho Kanakura and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo specializes in Indology and religious studies, having completed his PhD under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1976–1983). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1985–1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989–2013).
